# .github

## What it is

`.github/` holds CI, proof, release and repository-automation workflows under
`workflows/` and the issue/PR
templates ([[issue-intake.ava.okf.md]]).

GitHub-hosted runners: general CI and operational automation use
`ubuntu-24.04`, while app CI / release also use macOS 14 and Windows 2022. No self-hosted fleet, `container:`, or runner provisioner. Public-repo hosted minutes let the same CI
lane run for the canonical repo and forks without repository gating.

Each job provisions its own toolchain; [[ci-data-plane.ava.okf.md]] describes
the native database prerequisites and isolated test clusters.

## Core responsibilities

### `workflows/ci.yml` — the whole gate

Triggers: `pull_request` (every PR, no path filtering), `push` to `main`
(with `paths-ignore` for `ava_builtins/skills/**` and `**/*.md`), and
`workflow_dispatch`. Concurrency is keyed on the ref and cancels in-progress
runs for pull requests only, so a force-push supersedes its own earlier run
while main keeps every run.

Sharded fan-out behind stable check names, every job capped by
`timeout-minutes` so a hang cannot run to GitHub's global limit. A `classify`
job maps the PR diff through `base/deploy/git/repo_change.py` (the shared CI path
classifier) and gates the suites: docs-only skips both suites, frontend-only
skips backend, backend-only skips the frontend unit suite; e2e runs whenever
either side changed. Draft PRs skip CI until ready_for_review — except
Trunk test branches (`trunk-merge/*`, `trunk-temp/*`), which must verify.
The classifier recognizes component `docs/` layers containing `.ava.okf.md`
files, excluding test data. Trunk always sets the backend side so its full
suite remains reachable; non-PR runs set both sides. Independent documentation,
language, content-manifest and security gates still run for documentation PRs.

[[test-selection.ava.okf.md]] covers enforced backend selection; see
[docs/conventions/engineering/test-selection.md](../docs/conventions/engineering/test-selection.md).

The required Gitleaks job scans the complete Git history and working tree on
every eligible run, including docs-only changes; `.gitleaks.toml` is also the
local pre-commit policy, so fixture exceptions have one owner. A separate
dependency-audit job runs `uv audit --frozen` and `npm audit` as informational
checks while the remediation policy matures; its failure does not block the
workflow yet.

The informational merged-tree structure preview checks main's contribution to
the PR head; see [merged-tree lint](../docs/conventions/engineering/merged-tree-lint.md).

| CI check name | Composition |
|---|---|
| backend (pytest + pyright) | aggregator over `backend-static` (ruff, migration + clock-lattice lints, migration smoke, pyright and owned static pytest contracts with required JUnit, counts and coverage) + 16 pytest-split shards (`-n 4` each, least_duration (LPT)-balanced via the committed `.test_durations`, refreshed after 20 main changes with a nightly fallback by `.github/workflows/refresh-test-durations.yml`); combines per-shard coverage and applies the 85% line gate |
| backend structure (pre-commit lint + codegen freshness) | structure lint covers every eligible change class; Node/npm and four freshness hooks run on matching PR paths, selector errors and main pushes |
| frontend (eslint + tsc + vitest) | one job: `npm ci`, route typegen, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint with a warning baseline, `vitest run --coverage`, serial flaky lane |
| e2e (Playwright happy path) | aggregator over 4 shards, Playwright chromium `-n 2` each (browser dir cached) |

The backend test gate is fail-closed: [[test-gate.ava.okf.md]].

### `workflows/refresh-test-durations.yml` — nightly shard timing refresh

[[refresh-test-durations.ava.okf.md]] describes the isolated measurement and
review-only publication loop.

### `workflows/ci-app.yml` — path-filtered native app gate

Changes under `ui/app/` or the app release/test tooling run Rust format,
desktop clippy on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, an `aarch64` debug APK build after
applying the generated-project overlay, and the Android-overlay + updater-manifest
pytest files. The path filter keeps unrelated backend/frontend changes from
installing Tauri's native toolchain.

### `workflows/release-app.yml` — cross-platform app release

An `app-v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` tag builds a universal macOS DMG and Windows
NSIS installer. Complete secret groups activate Apple, Windows, and Tauri
updater signing; missing groups retain unsigned
build evidence. Signed updater archives become `latest.json`, published both
with the immutable version release and at the stable `app-latest` feed asset.
Manual dispatch builds without publishing.

### Action pinning

Every `uses:` is pinned to a **commit SHA** with the human-readable version in a
trailing comment. A moving tag like `@v6` is a mutable pointer the action's owner
can repoint at any time, which is a supply-chain write into every CI run.
`dependabot.yml` watches the `github-actions` ecosystem weekly so the pins are
updated by a reviewable PR rather than drifting silently or going stale.

### Repository automation and external-state audits

Proof workflow triggers, CI reruns, official-price proposals, and the weekly
branch-protection drift loop are detailed in [[repository-automation.ava.okf.md]].

## Key dependencies

- [[../tests/docs/tests.ava.okf.md]] — the suite the CI gates run.
- [[../scripts/docs/scripts.ava.okf.md]] — `ci_utils.py` polls a PR's CI to a verdict;
  release scripts create cluster notes and the app updater manifest; the branch
  audit compares GitHub's live protection state with `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- [[../ui/app/docs/app.ava.okf.md]] — native app built and released by the two
  app workflows.
- The hosted runner image supplies the base OS; everything Ava-specific is
  installed by the job's own steps, so a CI change never depends on out-of-band
  host state.

## Entry points

- Events: `pull_request`, `push` to main (`paths-ignore` for general CI and
  `paths` for app CI), `workflow_dispatch`, and
  `app-v*` app release tags, plus the daily model-pricing and weekly
  branch-protection schedules.
- Manual full run: `workflow_dispatch` on `ci.yml`.
- Local verification: lint/codegen at commit, heavy checks at pre-push, and
  targeted tests — see the [hook runbook](../docs/conventions/runbook.md#git-hooks-pre-commit--pre-push).

## Notes

- **Artifact publishing never gates.** Every `ci.yml` upload continues on error;
  coverage data retries once and records any missing shard explicitly.
- **CI owns the merge gate.** `backend-structure` partitions its commit-stage
  hooks into lint and conditional codegen; other jobs own excluded checks,
  except the local installation warning. The selector matches the base-to-HEAD
  diff against the four hooks' `files:` regexes in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
  Main pushes run codegen; the queue rechecks its combined tree. See the
  [runbook CI section](../docs/conventions/runbook.md#ci-continuous-integration).
- General CI's `paths-ignore` applies to `push` only; PR `classify` chooses
  suites, then [[test-selection.ava.okf.md]] governs backend subsets.
  Conservative fallbacks and Trunk merge-tree branches retain the full suite.
- Job names are surfaced to reviewers as check names; renaming one silently
  changes what a branch-protection rule matches.
- Duration refresh cadence and measured-versus-applied provenance: [policy](../scripts/ci/docs/duration-refresh.md).
